messages:
jessica_cs: Heads-up, BlinkPay says their ingest started failing immediately after last night's rollout. They provided examples; claim: responses no longer match their strict schema.

jessica_cs: Customer showed previous successful payload:
```
{
  "transaction_id": "abc123",
  "metadata": { "uuid": "f47ac10b58cc4372a5670e02b2c3d479" },
  "amount": 120.5
}
```
And what they're seeing now:
```
{
  "transaction_id": "abc123",
  "metadata": { "UUID": "F47AC10B-58CC-4372-A567-0E02B2C3D479" },
  "amount": "120.5",
  "trace": "TRACE=|user:blinkpay|req:0x9f8b...|..."
}
```
They said their parser requires lowercase metadata.uuid (32 hex chars, no hyphens) and numeric amount; the added top-level "trace" breaks strict contract.

emma_support: @jessica_cs do we know scope? single customer or wider?

jessica_cs: BlinkPay reports 100% of their calls failing post-rollout. No other customer reports yet but EU ops still coming online.

mike_sre: @nina_eng can you check recent response-postproc changes? Might be a decorator we shipped.

nina_eng: digging into git. I see PR #4821 added response tracing and a small uuid helper. Will verify behavior. :eyes: 

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary rollout completed -> service inference-response v2.1.7 @ 2026-03-16T23:18Z (canary 30% -> promoting)

oliver_prod: Confirmed PR #4821 toggled enable_response_tracing=true by default in the release. The tracing wrapper serializes payload to enable attaching trace metadata -> could be forcing uuid format and turning numbers to strings.

emma_support: Can we reproduce? Customer gave request_id req-0x9f8b. I replayed it on staging and saw the new format when tracing is on.

nina_eng: Repro on staging with enable_response_tracing=true. Root cause: tracing decorator does a json.dumps on the entire response, then parses it back, and in that path we run a uuid-canonicalize function that returns uppercase hyphenated uuids; also numeric values get converted to strings in some code paths.

mike_sre: Impact: strict schema consumers fail. BlinkPay P1. Immediate mitigation: disable tracing for production traffic while fix is prepared.

oliver_prod: Flipping the tracing flag off for canary group now; will rollback config to restore previous formatting. ETA ~10m.

deploy-bot: config change applied to canary group @ 2026-03-16T23:45Z

jessica_cs: Telling BlinkPay we've disabled tracing for their traffic. Will confirm once they test.

nina_eng: Plan: update tracing implementation to attach a separate "trace" object instead of reserializing the whole payload. PR #4835 submitted for type-safe tracing; tests added.

mike_sre: Temporary customer guidance: either accept stringified numbers or pin to previous model version; but best is disabling tracing until type-safe fix lands.

emma_support: @jessica_cs send BlinkPay this update and apologize. Offer to prioritize the fix and provide a timeline/credit if needed.

jessica_cs: Confirmed with customer: after we disabled tracing for their traffic their parser resumed normal behavior and failures stopped. They're asking for a post-mortem and timeline.

nina_eng: I'll include root cause and corrective actions in the post-mortem. Hotfix will keep tracing off by default; PR #4835 aims to preserve types and original uuid format.

oliver_prod: I'll watch production metrics and error rates. Also adding an integration test that fails builds if uuid format or numeric types change.

mike_sre: Add a lint/CI check in response-postproc to prevent accidental json.dumps of full payloads.

emma_support: Closing loop with BlinkPay; offering goodwill credits for downtime.

jessica_cs: Action items: Nina -> PR #4835 + tests; Oliver -> monitor; Mike -> update runbook/CI lint; Emma -> customer comms and credits.

mike_sre: Also adding a short-run incident doc to ensure faster CS/SRE/Handoffs next time.

jessica_cs: Filing the follow-up CS doc and will link the postmortem when available. :white_check_mark:
